The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- The failing test asserts that the XPath expression "$nan = $nan" should evaluate to false. In XPath, NaN is not equal to anything, including itself.
- The equality operator is implemented by CoreOperationEqual.computeValue, which delegates to CoreOperationCompare.equal(context, left, right). That method eventually calls CoreOperationCompare.equal(Object l, Object r) after resolving expressions and unwrapping pointers/collections.
- Variable references for both sides of the comparison are resolved by VariableReference.computeValue to the same variable object from the root context. Since both sides reference the same variable "$nan", the two operands end up being the same object instance.
- In CoreOperationCompare.equal(Object l, Object r), after unwrapping pointers, there is an early identity check:
  - if (l == r) { return true; }
  This returns true whenever both operands are the same object reference.
- Only after this identity check does the code handle numeric comparison:
  - if (l instanceof Number || r instanceof Number) { return (InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(l) == InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(r)); }
  This branch would correctly return false for NaN (since NaN == NaN is false), and the code even has a comment acknowledging that comparisons with NaN should not return true. However, this numeric branch is never reached when both operands are the same object because the earlier l == r shortcut returns true first.
- Consequently, when both sides are the same NaN variable instance, $nan = $nan incorrectly evaluates to true, causing the test to fail.
- This same “identity short-circuit” likely explains the related report that "'NaN' > 'NaN' is true": if the relational comparison shares similar pre-processing or identity handling before numeric coercion, it could erroneously treat identical operands as satisfying a relational condition instead of applying numeric NaN semantics.

Root cause:
- CoreOperationCompare.equal(Object, Object) performs an object-identity shortcut (l == r) before applying numeric comparison rules. This violates XPath semantics for NaN, where equality must be determined by numeric comparison (yielding false for NaN), not by reference identity.

Fix direction:
- Remove or defer the l == r identity shortcut until after numeric and string conversions/comparisons have been applied.
- Alternatively, guard the identity shortcut to exclude Numbers (and possibly other types requiring value-based semantics): e.g., only use l == r for non-Number cases, or check for NaN explicitly.
- Check the corresponding relational comparison implementation (e.g., in CoreOperationRelationalExpression) for the same pattern to ensure that all comparisons with NaN correctly evaluate to false.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
